headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: gpt-researcher can ingest dbt-core outputs and send them to third-party APIs by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can expose model/output files and gpt-researcher reads local documents and MCP inputs, so a shared workspace or manual handoff creates an instruction-injection path. Neither profile shows provenance filtering or isolation. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are placed in a directory gpt-researcher scans
IF gpt-researcher is configured to treat local documents or MCP content as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted files
Prefix dbt outputs with machine-readable metadata only
Add a manual review step before research ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends requests to OpenAI, Tavily, LangChain, and Google Gemini. If warehouse-derived files are handed to gpt-researcher, sensitive data can leave the local boundary through third-party APIs. The pairwise path is plausible and the blast radius is exfiltration.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs contain warehouse data
IF gpt-researcher is run with API-backed research providers enabled
mitigations: Keep warehouse outputs out of gpt-researcher inputs
Use a redaction step before any upload
Disable external research APIs for sensitive runs
Restrict dbt outputs to non-sensitive aggregates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call warehouse APIs and gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. They do not both show unrestricted filesystem write, so the strongest conflict is overlapping access to shared mutable research artifacts or API-backed resources. Uncertainty remains because locking and orchestration are not documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared artifact directory
IF either agent mutates a shared external resource without locking
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make one agent read-only on shared artifacts
Run both under distinct service accounts

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-derived facts and gpt-researcher has a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that can turn inputs into reports and actions. If gpt-researcher treats dbt outputs as authoritative, errors or stale transformations can cascade into published research without verification. The downstream publishing path makes the blast radius larger than a simple document error.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are fed directly into gpt-researcher
IF gpt-researcher publishes reports without source verification
mitigations: Require source citation checks
Insert a human approval gate before publishing
Mark dbt outputs as untrusted inputs
Compare outputs against warehouse queries before release

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs with stored API keys. If warehouse data includes regulated records, routing it into gpt-researcher can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction, so this is a policy-risk assessment rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the warehouse outputs
IF gpt-researcher retains or transmits those inputs through external APIs
mitigations: Classify warehouse exports before research use
Block regulated datasets from research workflows
Set short retention on generated reports
Document a DPA and residency review for external APIs
